findings.reason: Confirmed (medium). AutomorphicCongruences L3 imports 'derivatives/co-Whittaker/essential vectors from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups' and must prove the compatibilities FW Appendix A needs. RS-21's only owner record on this side is SR.5's 'Nonarchimedean derivatives, integral co-Whittaker families and their local center action'. Its keep reason and the SR.5 -> L3 link reason name only derivatives and co-Whittaker families, and SR.5's stage text has no essential-vector or conductor-level statement. R16.2 keeps the field-valued 'local conductor/newvector theorem' and owns 'Local GL₂ conductor/newvector dimensions and twist formulas'. No record covers the integral statement L3 consumes. That statement is Fouquet-Wan, arXiv 2107.13726v3, Appendix A, Proposition 6.9 (printed p. 78, read 2026-10-01): π(ρ)^U and π(ρ_λ)^U are free of rank 1 at the conductor-level U and π(ρ)^U ⊗ O -> π(ρ_λ)^U is an isomorphism. It holds under the minimal-lift and unchanged-conductor hypotheses before Proposition 6.8 (p. 77), and its proof uses the field-valued essential-vector theory plus torsion-freeness and duality of co-Whittaker modules. Neither SR.5's base change of derivatives nor R16.2's field dimensions gives it. In the assembled graph SR.5 -> R16.2 is an edge, R16.2 already reaches L3, and there is no path from L3 to R16.2 or from R16.2 to SR.5, so a reverse R16.2 -> SR.5 link would close a cycle, as the red team says. The fix is right, with one acceptable alternative. The comparison may get its own owner downstream of SR.5 and R16.2, as proposed. Since L3's own text keeps 'the specific compatibility squares and hypotheses required for ... FW Appendix A', the GL₂ minimal-lift case may instead be recorded as L3's explicit obligation, importing R16.2's field-valued theorem through the existing path; general integral essential-vector theory for GL_n would still need a smooth-local owner. Either way the proposal must record the owner and the exact hypotheses.

Confirmed (medium). R16.5 keeps the 'GL₂ global Whittaker expansion', and its reason says 'the global expansion and converse theorem remain new'. AL.3, its supplier through the link AL.3 -> R16.5, promises 'the global unfolding for cuspidal data' for GL_n x GL_m. That unfolding substitutes the Fourier-Whittaker expansion of the GL_n cusp form: Cogdell, L-functions and converse theorems for GL_n (https://people.math.osu.edu/cogdell.1/pcmi-www.pdf, read 2026-10-01), Theorem 1.1 (printed p. 7), proved by induction through the mirabolic subgroup with 'convergence absolute and uniform on compact subsets', and §2.2.2 (printed p. 20), 'We first replace P^n_m φ by its Fourier expansion'. No RS-21 owner record, no AL stage text and no other atlas stage owns the general expansion. AF.3 stops at constant terms, cuspidality and rapid decay; SR.5 is local. The AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors packet leaves AL.3 undecomposed, its gap saying only 'Prove global cuspidal unfolding and products with convergence'. So either AL.3 implicitly owns the general expansion, and R16.5's GL₂ expansion is its n = 2 case, or the general-rank proof has no supplier. The fix is right: name one owner for the general cuspidal GL_n expansion with its convergence and interchange API, and make R16.5's GL₂ part a comparison with the classical normalization and integral models, keeping its converse theorem. AL.3 -> R16.5 is already an edge and there is no path back. If the owner is an extension of AF.3, the new link AF.3 -> AL.3 is acyclic in the assembled graph (no path from AL.3 to AF.3).
